hook: SCP-122 is a star-shaped plastic night light that calms everyone within about twenty kilometres, as long as a devout young child sleeps in the room with it. At first the file reads gently, with a little girl's happy descriptions of her guardian angel. Pay attention to the details the cheerful tone glides past, and don't skip the footnotes.
whyItMatters: Its Thaumiel class matches how it is used: daily, as a tool, with Site-135's turnover and suicide rates depending on the light staying on. The article is built in two layers, a low-clearance version followed by a declassified one, so you read the same records twice with different information. That structure lets the reveal come from the document itself rather than from any added scene.
thingsToNotice:
The angel Anna describes moves closer each time, from beside the door to the edge of the bed to sitting right in front of her looking as if it wants a hug, and the declassified records put numbers on it: undetected, six metres, two metres, six centimetres, with more flickering each time. The expunged first entry turns out to be six-year-old Janna Marston, taken on her first night during a blackout, after which the Foundation simply noted the benefits, installed failsafes and found a new child.

The file ends with an emergency alert for a site-wide blackout and a last recovered image captioned "HE TELLS ME TO PRAY". Footnote four adds that the angel seen in staff dreams never shows this steady approach; the closing in happens only with the child.
